strings.name: Michelle Yeoh
strings.summary: Born in Ipoh, Malaysia, Michelle Yeoh trained in dance in Britain before entering Hong Kong cinema. Yes, Madam and Police Story III: Supercop established her as an action performer; Tomorrow Never Dies and Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon brought international attention. In 2023 she won the best actress Oscar for the 2022 film Everything Everywhere All at Once, becoming the first Asian woman to win that award. She has also participated in United Nations development initiatives.
strings.coverageNote: Selected dance training, representative films and the 2026 Berlin honorary award, checked through November 13, 2026; not a complete filmography or live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Building a cross-cultural career from Hong Kong action cinema to Everything Everywhere All at Once, she expanded the visibility of Asian women in international film.

strings.facts.f2.value: Studied dance and theatre in Britain
strings.highlights.h1.title: An Oscar milestone for Asian women
strings.highlights.h1.text: Won best actress for Everything Everywhere All at Once in 2023, the category’s first Asian female winner.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Across film traditions
strings.highlights.h2.text: Moved from Hong Kong action films into English-language cinema, with representative roles in Tomorrow Never Dies and Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Received Berlin’s Honorary Golden Bear
strings.timeline.t1.text: Received the Honorary Golden Bear at the opening of the 76th Berlinale for her career in cinema.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Won the best actress Oscar
strings.timeline.t2.text: Won for Everything Everywhere All at Once, released in 2022, becoming the first Asian woman to win the category.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Appointed UNDP Goodwill Ambassador
strings.timeline.t3.text: Accepted appointment as a Goodwill Ambassador, supporting the Sustainable Development Goals, gender equality and ending poverty.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Appeared in Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon
strings.timeline.t4.text: Played Yu Shu Lien in Ang Lee’s martial arts film, combining action performance with restrained characterization.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Appeared in Tomorrow Never Dies
strings.timeline.t5.text: Played Wai Lin in the James Bond film, widening English-speaking audiences’ recognition of her action performance.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Returned in Supercop
strings.timeline.t6.text: After a period away from films, appeared in Police Story III: Supercop and continued her action career.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Broke through with Yes, Madam
strings.timeline.t7.text: Following martial arts and stunt training, played a police inspector and established a recognizable presence in Hong Kong action cinema.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Continued dance training in Britain
strings.timeline.t8.text: Moved to Britain with her family at fifteen, studying dance at the Royal Academy of Dance alongside theatre training.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Born in Ipoh
strings.timeline.t9.text: Born in Ipoh, Perak, Malaysia; studied ballet as a child and later applied physical training to screen performance.
